profile.address: 44495, Gigabit Plaza, NTT Ashburn Campus, Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia, 20147
profile.reading:
This point is mapped as NTT Ashburn VA6 at 44495 Gigabit Plaza, Ashburn, VA, on the same Gigabit Plaza cluster as NTT's confirmed VA3, VA7, VA8, and VA9 buildings. NTT does not publish a dedicated facility page for VA6, and its own campus index and overview pages list only VA1, VA2, VA3, VA4, VA5, VA7, and VA11 as named, page-linked buildings; VA6 does not appear at all in NTT's own public materials, though the address itself comes from public geocoded property data placing a real structure at that location. This entry does not assert a square footage or MW figure it cannot confirm from NTT's own site. NTT describes its overall Ashburn campus as 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley," a figure that necessarily includes whatever capacity VA6 contributes, even though NTT does not break that figure out by building for every address on the campus.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which large-demand campus buildings like this one face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision. NTT's individually documented Ashburn buildings offer a scale reference for a typical building on this campus: VA1, a few blocks away at 44664 Guilford Drive, is confirmed by NTT's own site at 64,723 square feet of raised floor and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load, though this registry does not apply VA1's specific figures to VA6 since NTT has not confirmed the two buildings match. NTT's own building numbering on this campus runs at least through VA11, and several numbers, including this one, currently lack an individually published facility page despite OSM survey data placing a real, named structure at the mapped address.

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA6 is a 180,000 square foot facility completed in 2024 with 24 megawatts of published critical IT load. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 24 MW translates to approximately 600 racks of accelerator capacity. The building sits on NTT's larger 78-acre Ashburn campus, which publishes 224 megawatts of total critical IT load across multiple named buildings, though NTT does not break that figure out by individual facility. VA6 does not appear on NTT's own campus index pages despite its completion and confirmed address at 44495 Gigabit Plaza.

Virginia's regulatory environment now directly constrains expansion and operating economics for all Ashburn data centers. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that create a dedicated GS-5 rate class for large data center campuses, effective January 1, 2027, under which buildings like VA6 face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements. Residential electricity rates rose roughly $16 per month to offset the cost of this infrastructure build-out, making the grid constraint visible in household bills statewide.

Among Virginia's 23 facilities with published megawatt figures, VA6 ranks 24th individually, though it contributes to a campus that ranks far higher by aggregate capacity. The state has 330 mapped data center facilities overall, but only 23 publish power figures, and they total 1,375 megawatts. VA6's 24 megawatts represents 1.7 percent of Virginia's published capacity, a scale typical of the individual buildings that compose major regional hubs in Ashburn's "Data Center Alley."
